investigation_conclusion: On August 17, 2022, OCCL received a complaint regarding allegations of not feeding an infant appropriately. An investigation was conducted on August 19, 2022. Based on the results of this investigation, this complaint is substantiated because infant daily logs from August 10, 2022, and August 11, 2022, show Child #1 was not fed according to his monthly infant feeding schedule. The child was not fed the proper amount because he was transitioning from using a bottle to a cup and often refused the cup.

On February 5, 2024, the Office of Child Care Licensing (OCCL) received a complaint regarding lack of supervision and not notifying OCCL of a child's injury requiring medical attention. An investigation was conducted on February 9, 2024. Based on the results of this investigation there is no evidence to substantiate this complaint because the center administrator notified OCCL s intake worker on January 30, 2024, regarding Child #1 s accident/injury that occurred on January 29, 2024. Also, the center administrator stated she was not aware Child #1 was taken to the doctor for the second accident/injury because the child had not returned to care. There is no evidence to substantiate that children were not being properly supervised because the center administrator and Staff #1 both stated children were being supervised by two staff members at the time of the accident, but Child #1 was injured because he jumped off the steps.

On October 11, 2024, the Office of Child Care Licensing (OCCL) received a complaint regarding sanitation issues. An investigation was conducted on October 17, 2024. There is no evidence to substantiate this complaint for sanitation issues. After observations and interviews were conducted, the classrooms were clean, and sanitizing procedures are compliant with DELACARE Regulations.

On October 11, 2024, the Office of Child Care Licensing (OCCL) received a complaint regarding cell phone use by staff and not meeting the needs of children. An investigation was conducted on October 17, 2024. There is no evidence to substantiate this complaint for staff using cell phones while caring for children, or not meeting the needs of children. After speaking with administration and observing classrooms, staff members were actively engaged with the children and were not using cell phones. The administrator stated staff sometimes need to use cell phones to access the ProCare application when iPads are not working.

The Office of Child Care Licensing received a complaint on February 26, 2025, and additional information from the same Reporter on March 5, 2025, regarding allegations of failing to provide the required physical activity and outdoor play opportunities for children, incorrect staff-to-child ratios, not providing water to children as needed, and not following diapering procedures. An investigation was conducted on March 5, 2025. Based on the interviews, this complaint is substantiated for failing to provide the required physical activity and outdoor play opportunities for children. Two staff stated they have not gone outside since the end of last summer. Based on interviews and a review of attendance records, there is no evidence to substantiate this complaint for incorrect staff-to-child ratios, failing to provide water, or failing to follow diapering procedures. All documents reviewed showed classrooms maintained correct staff-to-child ratios. All staff interviewed stated water is available throughout the day in all classrooms. Classrooms were observed to have water available at the time of the visit. Documentation reviewed and staff interviews showed checking and changing of diapers is conducted as required.

investigation_result: No Evidence to Substantiate with Concern
investigation_conclusion: On July 11, 2025, the Office of Child Care Licensing received a complaint regarding failure to use positive behavior supports.  An investigation began on July 17, 2025, and concluded on July 30, 2025. The facility conducted an internal investigation and terminated the employment of Staff #1 on July 15, 2025, prior to the OCCL initial onsite complaint visit.  Based on a review of video footage, staff interviews, written statements, and internal investigation records, there is no evidence to substantiate this complaint for failure to use positive behavior supports. Additional concerns noted were although video recordings and staff statements document that Staff #1 did not make physical contact with Child #1, Staff #1 failed to be respectful and used a threatening action while interacting with Child #1. An additional concern noted was that Staff #1 was observed using a cell phone while caring for children.
